answer: Give every newcomer joint custody of one small shared reef pool, not a private plot. The pool holds tools, records, and a meadow of starter tasks strangers use. Each week the pool sends a public pulse: how many strangers it served, how well, and what broke. Privileges grow only while the pulse stays strong across a full season, and neighbours drawing from the pool can flag neglect. A farm spreading one operator across dozens of pools cannot keep every pulse healthy; neglected pools dry up, their keepers lose standing, and only fresh stranger-checked service restores them.
